problems.title: Lower curvature does not control explicit-step stability
problems.source_location: Proposition 1, Eqs.(3)â€“(4), PDF pp.6â€“7; Appendix B, p.22
claim: The proposition assumes \(-U\) is \(m\)-strongly convex and claims stability when \(\epsilon<[(1+2k_d)m]^{-1}\), then a unique stationary law with Gaussian noise.
analysis: On \(\mathbb R^2\), take \(-U=(x_1^2+10x_2^2)/2,m=1,k_d=1,\epsilon=1/10<1/3\). The second coordinate obeys \(z_{t+1}=-z_t+z_{t-1}\), with root \((-1-\sqrt5)/2\) of magnitude greater than one. Initial values \(z_{-1}=z_0=1\) yield \(1,1,0,1,-1,2,-3,\ldots\), and arbitrarily small scaled initial values still diverge. Gaussian forcing projects nontrivially onto the unstable mode. Any invariant characteristic function would satisfy \[|\phi(u)|\le\exp[-qu^2\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}r^{2j}/2]\to0\] for \(u\ne0\), contradicting continuity at zero.
result: The printed stability restriction and consequent invariant-law assertion are false even for a smooth globally strongly convex quadratic. No empirical benchmark failure follows.
repair: For quadratic Hessian \(H\succ0\), mode-wise Jury conditions give exactly \(0<\epsilon<2/[(1+2k_d)\lambda_{\max}(H)]\). This yields a unique invariant Gaussian for the stable linear augmented chain. Local nonlinear linearization does not itself prove global stochastic recurrence.

problems.title: Integral decay does not remove derivative feedback
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, PDF p.6; Algorithm 1, PDF p.7
claim: The text infers reduction to standard Langevin dynamics as \(k_i\to0\), although \(k_d\) remains positive.
analysis: For \(U=-x^2/2,k_i=0,k_d=1,\epsilon=0.1\), the limiting update is \(x_{t+1}=0.8x_t+0.1x_{t-1}+\sqrt{0.2}\xi_t\). Solving \(C=0.8V+0.1C\) and \(V=(0.8^2+0.1^2)V+0.16C+0.2\) gives \(V=180/187\), versus ordinary ULA variance \(20/19\). In stationarity \(\mathbb E[(x_t-x_{t-1})^2]>0\); stochastic derivative feedback does not vanish. The propositionâ€™s unnamed stationary law is not incorrectly attributed as the exact target.
result: The asserted transition reduction and its convergence inference are unsupported. Both fixed-step schemes can have discretization bias; this example does not show worse PID sample quality.
repair: State that vanishing integral control leaves proportional-derivative dynamics, whose stability and invariant law need separate analysis. Coefficient limits alone do not certify a time-varying sampler.

problems.title: The toy sampler uses a different integral and gain schedule
problems.source_location: Algorithm 1 and Section 3.3, PDF p.7; toy/Langevin.py, PID_ALD
claim: The paper uses a global running mean, carried annealing history and per-step integral decay; the toy source divides a finite window by its configured length, resets history each level and decays once per level.
analysis: With window length \(2\), the first integral is \(s/2\), versus the published \(s\). At step \(0.04\), gain \(0.2\), and maximum initial score magnitude \(2\), this alone changes the first state by \(0.008\), independently of coupled noise. For two steps per level, starting gain \(0.2\) and decay \(0.9\), the code uses \(0.2,0.2,0.18,0.18\), versus per-step \(0.2,0.18,0.162,0.1458\). The toy README documents a moving-window option; the image sampler has different history handling.
result: A local specification/release variant is established, without authenticating historical figure-generation settings or extending the discrepancy to every sampler.
repair: Either align the toy recurrence with Algorithm 1 or explicitly document the variant and exact experiment configurations. No restored empirical curve is claimed.
